content.text: {"title":"Softmax over the scores","narration":"We have scaled scores, but scores can be any size. Attention needs weights that are positive and add up to one. That is the job of softmax, applied to each row on its own. [[row0]]Take the first row: zero point five, zero, and one. Softmax raises e to each score, then divides by the total. That gives about zero point three one, zero point one nine, and zero point five one. [[row1]]The second row gives the same numbers, shifted: the biggest score, one, gets the biggest weight. [[row2]]And the third row puts its biggest weight on the first token. [[sums]]Every row now adds up to one, so each token's output is a weighted average of the values. Notice that softmax never gives a score zero weight, it only shrinks it. Try it yourself: edit the scores, then lower the temperature and watch each row sharpen, or raise it and watch the row
